population.definition: Ville de Kinshasa, 1984 scientific census (the last census held in the DRC); all later figures are projections

source.title: Portrait of Kinshasa: a city on (the) edge (Crisis States Working Paper 53.2)
source.author: Pascal Kapagama; Rachel Waterhouse
source.quote: A l’issue du recensement de 1984, l’effectif de la population de la ville de Kinshasa s’est élevé à 2.664.200 habitants

facts.claim: The last census in the DRC was held in 1984, so all population figures for Kinshasa are projection-based.

source.title: Profiling Living Conditions of the DRC Urban Population: Access to Housing and Services in Kinshasa Province
source.quote: the last being in 1984, all population figures for Kinshasa—either Kinshasa Province or Kinshasa City—are projection based

facts.claim: Léopoldville, originally Stanley Pool station, arose from Henry Morton Stanley's third expedition to the Congo (1879-1884).

source.title: Portrait of Kinshasa: a city on (the) edge (Crisis States Working Paper 53.2)
source.author: Pascal Kapagama; Rachel Waterhouse
source.quote: la ville de Léopoldville, actuellement Kinshasa, est née suite à la troisième expédition de Henry Morton Stanley au Congo (1879-1884)

facts.claim: Léopoldville is named after Leopold II, king of the Belgians, who commissioned the expeditions.

source.title: Portrait of Kinshasa: a city on (the) edge (Crisis States Working Paper 53.2)
source.author: Pascal Kapagama; Rachel Waterhouse
source.quote: Léopoldville vient du nom de Léopold II, roi des belges ayant commandité ladite expédition

facts.claim: The capital of the Congo was at Boma and was transferred to Léopoldville in 1929.

source.title: Portrait of Kinshasa: a city on (the) edge (Crisis States Working Paper 53.2)
source.author: Pascal Kapagama; Rachel Waterhouse
source.quote: Alors que la capitale du Congo se trouvait jusque là à Boma5, elle sera transférée à Léopoldville en 19296

facts.claim: Kinshasa lies on the bank of the Congo River at the exit of Pool Malebo and the start of the cataracts.

source.title: Portrait of Kinshasa: a city on (the) edge (Crisis States Working Paper 53.2)
source.author: Pascal Kapagama; Rachel Waterhouse
source.quote: Kinshasa est une ville tentaculaire située en bordure du fleuve Congo à la sortie du Pool Malebo et au début des puissantes chutes et cataractes

facts.claim: Before 1960 Kinshasa was a commercial centre before becoming an administrative capital.

source.title: Portrait of Kinshasa: a city on (the) edge (Crisis States Working Paper 53.2)
source.author: Pascal Kapagama; Rachel Waterhouse
source.quote: Avant 1960, Kinshasa était un centre commercial avant de devenir une capitale administrative

facts.claim: Léopoldville received civil status as a city, with annexed zones and 11 communes, in 1957.

source.title: Portrait of Kinshasa: a city on (the) edge (Crisis States Working Paper 53.2)
source.author: Pascal Kapagama; Rachel Waterhouse
source.quote: C’est en 1957 que Léopoldville recevra sa personnalité civile en tant que ville avec des zones annexes et composée de 11 communes

facts.claim: Kinshasa comprises 24 communes, of which Maluku, Nsele, Mont-Ngafula and Ngaliema are the largest.

source.title: Portrait of Kinshasa: a city on (the) edge (Crisis States Working Paper 53.2)
source.author: Pascal Kapagama; Rachel Waterhouse
source.quote: Kinshasa qui comprend actuellement 24 communes, dont Maluku, Nsele, Mont-Ngafula et Ngaliema sont les plus grandes

source.title: Portrait of Kinshasa: a city on (the) edge (Crisis States Working Paper 53.2)
source.author: Pascal Kapagama; Rachel Waterhouse
source.quote: En 1975, elle comptait 1.635.600 habitants

facts.claim: The DRC is preparing its second general population census, the first since 1984.

source.title: La RDC veut effectuer le premier recensement de sa population depuis 1984
source.quote: Le dernier remonte à 1984, soit près de 40 ans sans données démographiques complètes et actualisées

timeline.claim: The post of Léopoldville is dated to 1881, regarded as the starting point of the history of the city of Kinshasa.

source.title: Portrait of Kinshasa: a city on (the) edge (Crisis States Working Paper 53.2)
source.author: Pascal Kapagama; Rachel Waterhouse
source.quote: Lumenga Neso qui situe la création du poste de Léopoldville en 1881

timeline.claim: The capital of the Congo was transferred from Boma to Léopoldville in 1929.

source.title: Portrait of Kinshasa: a city on (the) edge (Crisis States Working Paper 53.2)
source.author: Pascal Kapagama; Rachel Waterhouse
source.quote: Alors que la capitale du Congo se trouvait jusque là à Boma5, elle sera transférée à Léopoldville en 19296

timeline.claim: Léopoldville received civil status as a city with 11 communes.

source.title: Portrait of Kinshasa: a city on (the) edge (Crisis States Working Paper 53.2)
source.author: Pascal Kapagama; Rachel Waterhouse
source.quote: C’est en 1957 que Léopoldville recevra sa personnalité civile en tant que ville avec des zones annexes et composée de 11 communes

timeline.claim: On 30 June 1966 President Mobutu proclaimed Patrice Lumumba a national hero and announced a large monument to him, the origin of the Limete Interchange.

source.title: RDC : l'Échangeur de Limete, un rêve monumental de Mobutu demeuré inachevé à Kinshasa
source.quote: L’idée de l’Échangeur de Limete remonte au 30 juin 1966, lorsque le Président Mobutu Sese Seko proclama Patrice Emery Lumumba héros national

timeline.claim: Work on the Limete Interchange was interrupted between 1974 and 1978.

source.title: RDC : l'Échangeur de Limete, un rêve monumental de Mobutu demeuré inachevé à Kinshasa
source.quote: L’interruption des travaux entre 1974 et 1978 demeure l’un des épisodes les plus controversés de l’histoire de l’Échangeur de Limete

timeline.claim: The 1984 census counted 2,664,200 people in the city of Kinshasa.

source.title: Portrait of Kinshasa: a city on (the) edge (Crisis States Working Paper 53.2)
source.author: Pascal Kapagama; Rachel Waterhouse
source.quote: A l’issue du recensement de 1984, l’effectif de la population de la ville de Kinshasa s’est élevé à 2.664.200 habitants

timeline.claim: A partial rehabilitation in 2011 installed the Museum of Contemporary and Multimedia Art and a 6.5 m statue of Lumumba at the foot of the Limete tower.

source.title: RDC : l'Échangeur de Limete, un rêve monumental de Mobutu demeuré inachevé à Kinshasa
source.quote: En 2011, une réhabilitation partielle permit notamment l’installation du Musée d’art contemporain et multimédia

timeline.claim: The Académie des Beaux-Arts, founded in 1943, celebrated its 75th anniversary in 2018.

source.title: RDC: l'Académie des Beaux-Arts fête ses 75 ans
source.quote: Fondée en 1943 par Frère Marc Stanislas Wallenda, l'Académie des Beaux-Arts de Kinshasa souffle cette année ses 75 bougies

timeline.claim: The Limete Interchange Tower became the logo of the 9th Jeux de la Francophonie, held in Kinshasa from 26 July to 6 August 2023.

source.title: Jeux de la Francophonie: à la découverte de la Tour Échangeur de Limete, monument symbole de Kinshasa
source.author: Christian Nyamabu Kabeya
source.quote: symbolise aujourd’hui le logo des 9èmes jeux de la francophonie organisés à Kinshasa du 26 juillet au 6 août 2023

places.name: Virunga National Park
places.what: Virunga was set up in 1925 as Parc National Albert, the first national park in Africa, and became a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1979. It protects mountain gorillas and other great apes.

facts.label: Established
facts.value: 1925, as Parc National Albert; Africa's first national park

source.title: History - Visit Virunga
source.quote: It was set up in 1925 as Parc National Albert and thus became the first national park in Africa, gaining its UNESCO designation in 1979

facts.label: Founder
facts.value: King Albert I of Belgium

source.title: History - Visit Virunga
source.quote: The park was founded by King Albert I of Belgium and originally known as Albert National Park

facts.label: Wildlife
facts.value: Home to three taxa of great apes and one-third of the world's remaining mountain gorillas

source.title: Virunga National Park (official site)
source.quote: Home to three taxa of great apes ... Home to one-third of the world's remaining mountain gorillas

facts.label: Area
facts.value: About 7,800 km² (3,000 square miles)

source.title: Rangers Killed in Africa's Oldest Park Push Death Toll to 150
source.quote: The 3,000-square-mile (7,800 square kilometers) reserve was established in 1925 as Africa's first national park

facts.label: Danger
facts.value: UNESCO changed the site's status to 'endangered' after the park lost control to militias

source.title: History - Visit Virunga
source.quote: UNESCO changed the World Heritage Site status to “endangered.”

places.name: Lola ya Bonobo
places.what: Lola ya Bonobo is a sanctuary near Kinshasa where orphaned bonobos rescued from the illegal wildlife trade find care. Its operator describes it as the world's only bonobo sanctuary.

facts.value: Orphaned bonobos rescued from the illegal wildlife trade find safety and comfort

source.title: Friends of Bonobos / Lola ya Bonobo
source.quote: At Lola ya Bonobo sanctuary, orphaned bonobos rescued from the illegal trade in wildlife find safety and comfort

facts.label: Uniqueness
facts.value: Described as the world's only bonobo sanctuary

source.title: Friends of Bonobos / Lola ya Bonobo
source.quote: World’s only bonobo sanctuary

facts.label: Approach
facts.value: Rescue, sanctuary and rewilding of endangered bonobos

source.title: Friends of Bonobos / Lola ya Bonobo
source.quote: We provide rescue, sanctuary and rewilding to endangered bonobos
